subject: general
question: Which committee recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj structure in the Indian constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Balwant Rai Mehta Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee** was formed in **1957** to examine the working of the Community Development Programme (1952) and the National Extension Service (1953).
 
• The Committee recommended the establishment of a **three-tier Panchayati Raj system** in India to promote decentralization and democratic governance at the grassroots level.
 
• The three-tier structure proposed by the Committee consisted of:
 
 
• **Gram Panchayat** at the village level.
 
• **Panchayat Samiti** at the block level.
 
• **Zila Parishad** at the district level.
 
 
 
• The Committee advocated for the Panchayati Raj institutions to serve as **instruments of rural development** and involve local people in decision-making.
 
• The recommendations of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee were implemented in **1959**, with Rajasthan being the first state to launch the Panchayati Raj system, followed by Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Committee emphasized the need for **democratic decentralization** to achieve effective governance and development at the grassroots level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Features of the Panchayati Raj System:**

 
 
• The system is based on the principle of **decentralization of power**, ensuring that decisions are made at the lowest possible level.
 
• The three-tier structure consists of elected representatives at each level to ensure **participatory governance**.
 
• The primary functions of Panchayati Raj institutions include **planning and implementing development programmes**, resolving local disputes, and promoting social justice.
 
• The Panchayati Raj system is governed by the provisions of the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, which gave it constitutional status.
 
• Key provisions of the 73rd Amendment include **mandatory elections**, reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women, and the establishment of a State Election Commission.
 
 
 
• **Other Committees Related to Panchayati Raj:**
 
 
• **Ashok Mehta Committee (1977):** Recommended a two-tier system and suggested measures to strengthen Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• **GVK Rao Committee (1985):** Highlighted the need for decentralized planning and development through Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• **LM Singhvi Committee (1986):** Recommended constitutional recognition for Panchayati Raj institutions, which was later implemented through the 73rd Amendment.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, is a landmark reform in Indian governance that institutionalized the Panchayati Raj system.
 
• Panchayati Raj institutions play a crucial role in promoting **rural development**, ensuring **social justice**, and empowering local communities.
 
• The system has been instrumental in implementing various government schemes like **MGNREGA** and **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** at the grassroots level.
